title: How and Why You Should Spatchcock Your Turkey
summary: Taking the backbone out and splaying out your bird yields evenly cooked meat almost every time.
body_markdown:

By[Krysten Chambrot](https://cooking.nytimes.com/author/krysten-chambrot)


Published Nov. 16, 2026


Updated Nov. 16, 2026


Ask a food professional about the best way to cook a turkey, and spatchcocking is bound to come up. But what sounds quirky and complicated is actually quite straightforward and simple.


For an oddly shaped bird, like the turkey, whose breast is especially large and close to the heat source, the technique helps ensure more even cooking and expedites the process — no more waiting for the legs to brown after the breast is cooked.


To spatchcock is to cut out the bird’s backbone and press the bird flat.


## Watch Samin Nosrat demonstrate how to spatchcock


Samin Nosrat shows how to spatchcock a turkey for quicker roasting.


Credit...


The New York Times Cooking


### Spatchcocking Instructions


1. Pull out the neck and giblets from the bird’s cavity and ensure it is otherwise empty.


2. Turn the bird breast-side down, and, with kitchen shears or a knife, remove the backbone by cutting through the bones on each side. The chef and cookbook author Samin Nosrat suggests alternating cuts from top and bottom.


3. With the backbone removed and the open cavity facing you, use your body weight to press the two sides of the birds open like a book. You’ll hear some cracking, and that’s a good thing. Then, it’s simply a matter of turning the bird right side up and placing it on a sheet tray to roast.
